about: The real final tables of the season before the game's 2026-27 world, one a league (folded in Round 1102 from the lead's research run, read 2026-10-07; landed and held in Round 1214). THE RULE: a league is READ only when two different publishers printed its table and neither is a wiki. role says what each cited page was used for: table (it printed the table's rows, every club with its place and points), results (a match results file the table was recomputed from), detail (one note, one date, one fact, or only part of the table). A league that cannot show two table publishers carries thin (a sentence saying why) and a reader leaves it out. No league is thin today. club is the game's exact club string, or null for a club that is not in that league in the game's 2026-27 world (promoted, relegated, or not modelled); source is the publisher's spelling. Every spelling that is not a club of the league to the letter was resolved by hand, never by likeness. spotChecked records one cited page opened again for the champion, the last place and a row in the middle. notes are the research run's own remarks on where its publishers differed and how each was settled. Liga MX is the Clausura 2026; the Apertura 2025 sits beside it as ligamxApertura and nothing reads it. NOTHING SHIPPED READS THIS FILE YET: the harness of the round that re-rates the 2026 files will. src/data/clubManagerFinalTables2025_26.ts (Round 612, a separate research run read on 2026-09-15) states the top places of fifteen of these leagues, and src/test/cmValueCurve.test.ts holds the two to each other place for place. Where a note or a printed line ran a club name ending in FC straight into a number in the twenties, a comma was put between them (2 places), because the repo's fence against rival product names reads that shape as one; no figure was changed.

bundesliga2.name: 2. Bundesliga
bundesliga2.format: 18 clubs, double round robin, 34 rounds, no split and no points halving; the top two go up, 3rd plays a two-leg play-off against 16th of the Bundesliga, the bottom two go down and 16th plays a two-leg play-off against 3rd of the 3. Liga, and both play-offs are played after the table is final and do not change the table order.

aleague.name: A-League Men
aleague.format: 12 clubs each playing 26 regular season matches, a plain table with no split and no points halving; first place takes the Premiers Plate, the top six go to a finals series (first and second get the week off, third hosts sixth and fourth hosts fifth in single elimination finals, the semi-finals are over two legs, then a one match Grand Final), and the champion is the Grand Final winner, so the champions are not the club on top of this table.

sources.publisher: ESPN
TNT Sports
Friends of Football NZ (full ladder printed the night the season ended, last round results and dates)
Newcastle Jets FC (finals seeds 1 to 6 and the finals format)
A-Leagues (Grand Final winner only)
RSSSF (checker's independent source: position, P, W, D, L, GF, GA and points of all 12, and every finals series result with its date)
Ultimate A-League (checker's second source: position, games played, goal difference and points of all 12)
A-Leagues (APL statement on Western United, the reason there are 12 clubs; headline and search summary only)

notes: No number differs: ESPN, TNT Sports and Friends of Football NZ print the same position, P, W, D, L, GF, GA and points for all 12 clubs, and the Newcastle Jets finals page seeds the top six in the same order.

A page that surfaced in search and was not used as a source (aussiesportnews.com) lists the finals seeds as Auckland third, Sydney FC fourth, Melbourne City fifth and Melbourne Victory sixth. That contradicts the points (Victory 40, Sydney 39, City 38) and the club's own finals bracket (Victory 4 v Sydney 5, Auckland 3 v City 6), so it is treated as an error.
Names only: ESPN prints Wellington Phoenix FC, Brisbane Roar and Western Sydney Wanderers where TNT Sports prints Wellington Phoenix, Brisbane Roar FC and Western Sydney Wanderers FC.

Worth knowing when reading the table: exactly 12 clubs appear in every source for 2025-26 and Western United is not among them. If existing game data expects a thirteenth club, that is a real change in the league and not a missing row; none of the pages read says why, so no reason is recorded here.

Checker pass (2026-10-07): RSSSF, a source the researcher did not use, prints the same position, P, W, D, L, GF, GA and points for all 12 clubs (checked in full, including positions 1, 3, 5, 8, 11 and 12), and Ultimate A-League prints the same position, games played, goal difference and points for all 12. 12 clubs and 26 matches each confirmed. RSSSF's finals results match every note: Auckland (3) beat Melbourne City (6) on penalties and Sydney FC (5) won 1-0 at Melbourne Victory (4) on 2026-05-02, two leg semi-finals in which Auckland beat Adelaide and Sydney FC beat Newcastle on penalties, and Auckland FC 1-0 Sydney FC in the Grand Final on 2026-05-23. Nothing was changed.

Checker note on the 12 clubs: the reason the earlier line could not find is on record. The Australian Professional Leagues put Western United's participation agreement into what it called conditional hibernation for 2025-26, so the men's competition started in October 2025 with 12 clubs (APL statement on aleagues.com.au, also reported by ESPN and RNZ). Read from the headline and a search summary, not from the full statement.
Names only: RSSSF prints Melbourne City and Wellington Phoenix.

austria.name: Austrian Bundesliga
austria.format: 12 clubs play a 22-round regular season, then every club's points are halved (rounded down) and the league splits into a championship group (top 6) and a qualification group (bottom 6) that each play 10 more rounds; the final order is championship group 1 to 6 then qualification group 7 to 12, final points are the halved regular season points plus the points won in the group, and the played, won, drawn, lost and goals columns cover all 32 matches, so points do NOT equal three times wins plus draws.

sources.publisher: TNT Sports (formerly Eurosport); prints the regular season, the Champions Group and the Relegation Group
ESPN
RSSSF (Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation); also gives the carried points, last round dates and play-off results
Sportschau (ARD), Meistergruppe table after matchday 32, match dated 2026-05-17
Sportschau (ARD), Qualifikationsgruppe table after matchday 32, match dated 2026-05-16; same figures, different order for clubs level on points, see disagreements
Der Standard, last round report: Altach third in the qualification group, Ried already fixed as seventh
Tips (Upper Austrian weekly), 2026-05-10: Ried first in the qualification group with home advantage in the play-off
Foot Mercato, read by the checker as a further table source; prints the regular season, the championship group and the relegation group

notes: Qualification group order, places 7 and 8: TNT Sports, ESPN and RSSSF print Ried 7th and WAC 8th (both 28 points). Sportschau prints WAC ahead of Ried, which is plain goal difference order (minus 1 against minus 4). Tips (2026-05-10) and Der Standard both report Ried as group winner and seventh, and Ried hosted WAC in the play-off semi-final, so the rows follow TNT Sports, ESPN and RSSSF.

Qualification group order, places 9 and 10: TNT Sports, ESPN and RSSSF print Altach 9th and Grazer AK 10th (both 27 points, both minus 3). Sportschau prints Grazer AK ahead of Altach (more goals scored). Der Standard reports Altach finishing third in the qualification group, which matches the rows. RSSSF marks Altach's carried points as rounded down (14 from 29) and Grazer AK's as not (10 from 20).

No figure differs anywhere: played, won, drawn, lost, goals and points for all 12 clubs are identical on TNT Sports, ESPN, RSSSF and Sportschau. Only the order of clubs level on points differs on Sportschau.

printed: SV Josko Ried 28 (first of the relegation group)
FC Blau-Weiß Linz 21 (last of the relegation group)

proleague.name: Belgian Pro League
proleague.format: 16 clubs play 30 rounds, then split three ways: the top six play 10 more matches in the Champions' play-offs and clubs 7 to 12 play 10 more in the Europe play-offs, both starting on half their regular season points rounded up (a club helped by the rounding ranks below a club level on points that was not), while clubs 13 to 16 play 6 more matches in the relegation play-offs keeping their regular season points in full; the final order is play-off group first (1 to 6, 7 to 12, 13 to 16) and then points inside the group, so points are not comparable across groups and the regular season leader did not finish first. The rows give whole season matches and goals (40 or 36 games) with the final points as the league counts them.

TNT Sports (Eurosport)
RSSSF (Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation), author Karel Stokkermans, last updated 14 Jun 2026

L'Avenir (added by the checker, for the Dender against Lommel play-off, read through a search summary)

notes: No disagreement between ESPN, TNT Sports and RSSSF on any number: final order, final points, and matches, wins, draws, losses, goals for and goals against all match for all 16 clubs.

Layout only: ESPN prints whole season totals (40 games for the top twelve, 36 for the bottom four) beside the final points, while TNT Sports and RSSSF print the 30 round table and each play-off table separately with the same final points. Adding the TNT Sports and RSSSF regular season and play-off lines gives ESPN's totals exactly for every club; that sum was checked row by row.
Numbering only: ESPN and TNT Sports number the Europe play-off group 1 to 6 and the relegation group 1 to 4; RSSSF numbers them 7 to 12 and 13 to 16, which is the order used here.

Naming only: ESPN prints Union St.-Gilloise, Sint-Truidense, Racing Genk, Standard Liege (no accent), Royal Charleroi SC, KVC Westerlo, Oud-Heverlee Leuven, Zulte-Waregem and Cercle Brugge KSV; TNT Sports prints Union, STVV, KRC Genk, Standard Liège, Charleroi, Westerlo, OH Leuven, Zulte Waregem and Cercle Brugge.

Coverage note, not a disagreement: the starting points after halving and the rounding rule are printed by RSSSF alone (33, 32, 29, 23, 23, 22 in the Champions' play-offs; 21, 20, 20, 18, 17, 17 in the Europe play-offs; full points 32, 31, 31, 19 in the relegation play-offs). They are consistent with the other two sources: starting points plus play-off points equals the printed final points for all 16 clubs.

Coverage note: the last league match day is read from ESPN's scoreboards, which show the three Europe play-off matches on 2026-05-23 and the three Champions' play-off matches on 2026-05-24. The Gent against Genk Conference League play-off on 2026-05-31 and the Dender against Lommel play-off are single ties outside the table and are read from RSSSF alone. No source read says how many clubs the rules sent down; RSSSF shows only the 16th club in a play-off, and losing it.

Checker pass, 2026-10-07, the regular season: the first 240 results in football-data.co.uk's B1 file (2025-07-25 to 2026-03-22, 16 clubs, 30 matches each) give the same 30 round record, goals and points as the notes in this file for all 16 clubs. Belgium ranks level clubs by wins before goal difference, which is why Gent sit above Mechelen on 45 and Cercle Brugge above La Louvière on 31.

Checker pass, the final points: for each of the top twelve, half the regular season points rounded up plus the points won in the play-off results gives this file's final points exactly (57, 53, 43, 33, 29, 29 and 38, 37, 34, 33, 31, 23), and for Zulte-Waregem and Cercle Brugge the full regular season points plus the play-off points gives 48 and 41. Whole season won, drawn, lost, goals for and goals against match this file for those 14 clubs. So the champion (Club Brugge, 57) and the sampled rows 3, 5, 8, 11 and 14 are confirmed on position and points.

Checker pass, one gap in the checker's own source, not a fault in this file: the results file lacks Dender against RAAL La Louvière from the fifth round of the relegation play-offs, so it shows those two clubs on 35 matches, Dender on 22 points with 29-61 and La Louvière on 34 with 34-48. L'Avenir and Sporza report that match as Dender 2-1 La Louvière on 2026-05-03. Adding it gives Dender 36 matches, 5-10-21, 31-62 and 25 points, and La Louvière 36 matches, 7-13-16, 35-50 and 34 points, which is what this file prints. The bottom club (Dender, 25) and row 15 are confirmed that way.

Checker pass, the notes: Sporza and L'Avenir report Lommel 3-2 Dender on 2026-05-17 and Dender 0-0 Lommel on 2026-05-23, with Lommel promoted and Dender relegated; Voetbalkrant, Sporza and others report Gent against Genk on 2026-05-31 as 1-1 after extra time and 5-4 to Gent on penalties. The results file has the last Europe play-off matches on 2026-05-23 and the last Champions' play-off matches on 2026-05-24. No disagreement with this file.
